summary: This manuscript reports a preregistered, deterministically executed paired experiment that tested whether embedding a reachability/policy verifier in a generate–verify–repair (GVR) loop reduces security-relevant (forbidden-reachability) misconfigurations from an LLM-based intent→configuration pipeline. The run completed as preregistered (N=300 matched pairs) under a shared_initial_candidate contract (one LLM generation per pair, replayed to both arms). All 300 pairs passed the forbidden-reachability predicate in both arms; validators never flagged a violation and no repair calls were invoked. The authors archive extensive execution, validator, and analysis artifacts and draw operational design lessons about generation semantics, adversary potency, and verifier strength. The experiment and artifact accounting appear to be executed and archived consistently with the preregistration. However, the confirmatory test of repair efficacy is rendered uninformative by two coupled design outcomes (shared replay semantics and zero observed baseline violations). The manuscript contains strong reproducibility evidence but reads partially as an artifact-inventory; it needs clearer, conventional scholarly framing and concise technical definitions of the verifier predicate and validators so readers can assess construct validity.
critical_issues: Primary-inference mismatch: the preregistered confirmatory hypothesis (repair efficacy) is effectively untestable given (a) the shared_initial_candidate replay semantics (baseline is not an independent-generation arm) which reduces between-arm variance, and (b) zero observed baseline violations. The manuscript must explicitly and prominently state that the primary confirmatory hypothesis was not tested (untestable) and that the observed result is a degenerate null that only bounds the baseline violation rate.

Manuscript presentation is metadata/provenance-heavy: substantial sections list artifact paths, hashes and manifest content inline rather than providing concise methods and results written as standard scholarly prose. This reduces readability and risks the paper being judged an artifact report rather than a conference short paper. The paper must be rewritten to prioritize narrative methods/results/interpretation and compress provenance pointers.

Construct clarity for the key predicate is insufficient: the manuscript does not give a concise, standalone technical definition of the 'forbidden-reachability' predicate and the concrete capabilities/limitations of the two deterministic validators (what they check, their oracle assumptions, false-negative risks). Readers need a brief, precise description in the Methods (the artifacts may be cited for full detail).

Overclaiming risk: some wording implies broader operational generality (e.g., about verifier usefulness) despite the degenerate result and single-model, synthetic-emulation scope. The conclusions must be toned to match the evidence and limitations already archived.
required_revisions: Revise abstract, introduction (end-of-intro contribution bullets), and conclusion to state unambiguously and prominently that the preregistered confirmatory hypothesis about repair efficacy was untestable in this run (explain that shared_initial_candidate + zero baseline violations produced a degenerate contingency) and that the paper's main empirical contribution is deterministic execution accounting, artifact archiving, and design/engineering lessons for follow-up stress tests. Update any language that could be read as evidence that verifiers 'reduce' misconfigurations.

Replace long inline provenance inventories with concise scholarly prose. Move the exhaustive artifact-path/hash listings out of the main narrative: condense to a short sentence such as 'Full execution, validator, and analysis artifacts (hash manifest and paths) are archived in the evidence bundle; representative artifact identifiers are cited.' Keep at most one short paragraph listing the most important artifact filenames/sha256 values needed to verify key claims. (All referenced artifacts are already available in the supplied bundle.)

Add a concise technical subsection (≤1 paragraph) in Methods that defines the forbidden-reachability predicate precisely (what reachability pairs/policies are tested, whether ACL/route-policy semantics are included, what constitutes a violation) and that summarizes each validator's detection model (Batfish-style execution validator: what execution semantics are checked; static reachability analyzer: its algorithmic assumptions). Cite the per-episode validator_trace artifacts for full details and avoid reproducing raw logs in the narrative.

Edit the Discussion and Limitations to (a) explicitly connect how the shared_initial_candidate contract affects inferential power (quantify that baseline was replayed), (b) remove or reword any statements implying repair efficacy, and (c) present the Clopper–Pearson bound and its interpretation as the proper descriptive outcome of the run. Ensure these clarifications are present in the abstract and contributions list so a reader cannot misinterpret the result.

Condense or reformat the Results section so that the statistical findings (contingency table, McNemar test p-value, bootstrap CI, Clopper–Pearson upper bound) are presented as a compact narrative plus one small table or figure; keep extended numerical/artifact evidence only in the archived artifacts referenced concisely.
optional_revisions: Include a short evidence-to-claim table (one page at most, or a compact paragraph) mapping each principal claim to the exact archived artifact(s) that support it (the manuscript already archives these artifacts; a compact table improves clarity).

Add an explicit short paragraph that compares the present design trade-offs (shared vs independent draws) with an independent-generation confirmatory variant, with example model-call budgets estimated from the execution manifest to help practitioners plan follow-up runs.
Tidy figure captions and compress or remove redundant artifact pointers from caption text (retain citations to the single canonical artifact manifest).
